question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births registered in Taiwan in September 2026, as reported in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics.

target.what: Number of live births registered in Taiwan (Republic of China) during September 2026, as counted in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics (births registered in the month, by date of registration)
target.publisher: Ministry of the Interior (MOI), Republic of China (Taiwan) — Department of Household Registration monthly statistics
target.cadence: monthly, typically published in the following month (preliminary), with revisions
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-08 cutoff, so no September 2026 figure exists yet; must be projected. Definition is registration-based (date of registration), not date of occurrence, so late registrations and reporting lags matter. Working interpretation: total births registe

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 births registered will follow the recent monthly level and September seasonal pattern; the most recent published months (through ~July/August 2026) anchor the level, and prior Septembers give the seasonal factor.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly registered births for Taiwan for each month from 2023 through the latest month published before 2026-09-08 (ideally Jan–Jul/Aug 2026), plus September values for 2023, 2024, 2025 to estimate a September seasonal ratio (Sept / trailing 3-month average). Minimum: last 12 monthly values and the last 3 September values.

assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 registration level tracks the 2026 YoY decline seen in July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: August 2026 births showing a sharp rebound or further collapse relative to 2025.

assumptions.name: September share of annual births

assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a strong September seasonal spike or trough in 2026.

methods.label: m1

p95.role: Registered births in Taiwan, September 2025 (month of registration)

a1.role: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Repaired m1: yoy_scaling could not execute because no 2026 signal exists. Recast as formula_mc using the official RIS September 2025 anchor (p95 = 8,603) times the observed 2026 YoY decline factor a1 (~0.90). Shared dependency: relies on the 2026 decline persisting into September; failure mode is a policy-driven rebound from the 2026 birth subsidy.

methods.label: m2

p53.role: NDC projected full-year 2026 total live births (94,000)

methods.rationale: NDC full-year 2026 projection (p53) times September's share of annual births (a2). Independent of the monthly registration series; anchors on the annual projection which already embeds the observed Jan-Jul 2026 level (p52).

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Monthly registration series Jan 2025 through July 2026 (p100-p107, p95-p98, p18, p19, p17). With 15 consecutive months, code uses AutoETS/Theta/YoY/LightGBM ensemble to forecast September 2026 from the recent level and September seasonal pattern. Shared dependency: same MOI registration series as m1.

series_auto.rule: yoy3: last year's same month x the summed growth of the latest 3 year-on-year pairs

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: this block is the median
weight_basis.m2: B2 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)
weight_basis.m3: B3 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m1.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

baseline.rule: seasonal naive: the target's value for the same month last year

kept.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025
kept.rationale: Recent 2026 months run below 2025: July 2026 was -11.56% YoY (p20/p223), and the 2026 level (Jan-Jul ~54,000, p52) is well below 2025. September 2025 was 8,603 (p95). A factor near 0.90 with wide range reflects the observed ~10-12% decline plus uncertainty.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 continues the 2026 YoY decline seen in July.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 births have stabilized or rebounded to 2025 levels.

kept.name: September share of annual births
kept.rationale: September 2025 was 8,603 of 107,812 annual (p95/p99) ≈ 0.0798; typical September share is near 1/12 ≈ 0.083. Range covers seasonal variation.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 has a similar seasonal share as prior years.
kept.falsified_by: A large shift in the seasonal birth pattern.

published.note: not checked: backtest or scored question (as_of before today, or an official value is registered), so the target cannot have been published by as_of

Method m1 scales the September 2025 anchor by an assumed YoY factor 0.9 (range 0.78 to 1.02); m2 applies an assumed September share 0.083 (range 0.05874 to 0.1175) to the annual projection; m3 extrapolates the registration series. Code combined three non-overlapping blocks with equal weight per block, taking the median; widths came from default, Monte Carlo, and benchmark calibration, not backtest errors.

- a1 September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025: 0.9 [n], range 0.78 to 1.02; used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that 2026 births have stabilized or rebounded to 2025 levels.
- a2 September share of annual births: 0.083 [n], range 0.05874 to 0.1175 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: A large shift in the seasonal birth pattern.

- m1 formula_mc: p95 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 6,105 to 9,633; result unit (birth/month) * 1 month converted to birth; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m2 formula_mc: p53 * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 5,273 to 11,580; result unit (birth/month) * 1 month converted to birth; own 80% width x/÷1.48 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m3 series_auto, yoy path: yoy3: last year's same month x the summed growth of the latest 3 year-on-year pairs. - Combination: 3 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 7,665 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m2: 7,806 (width x/÷1.48, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B3 = m3: 7,206 (width x/÷1.23, benchmark calibration). by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
